paragraphs: Friend, this one is heavy, so let's just say it. The flock in this passage is marked for slaughter, and the people who should be looking after it have "no compassion on them" (Zechariah 11:5). The LORD says He will no longer have compassion on the people of the land (Zechariah 11:6). The lesson is that God sees how His flock gets treated, and what He does about it matters.

Now look at the two staffs, Favor and Union. When they get cut in two, the covenant with all the nations is revoked and the brotherhood between Judah and Israel is broken (Zechariah 11:10, 14). I think that's the part to carry with you, baker: when people turn away from the Shepherd, things come apart. And still, the afflicted of the flock who were watching knew "it was the word of the LORD" (Zechariah 11:11).

Then there's the price. The flock weighs out "thirty pieces of silver," and the LORD calls it "this magnificent price at which they valued me" (Zechariah 11:12-13). The passage ends with a woe on the worthless shepherd "who deserts the flock" (Zechariah 11:17). So here's what I'd bake into your heart today: a true shepherd stays with the flock, and God takes it seriously when a shepherd doesn't. And this story isn't over, friend.
